title: Test the boundary
summary: Return None for division by zero and test the ordinary and boundary cases.

scenario.briefing: A reporting function divides totals by counts. The empty case must return None instead of crashing the report.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Return None for the zero case.
Keep the ordinary division for everything else.

misconceptions.description: Catching every exception to hide failures.
misconceptions.feedback: Catch the specific failure you can handle. A broad catch hides programming errors.

misconceptions.description: Treating a test that merely runs as a passing test.
misconceptions.feedback: A test must assert the expected result. Running without an exception proves only that no exception was raised.

sections.title: A test asserts a specific result
sections.body: A useful test arranges the input, calls the function, and asserts the exact result. Running code without an assertion proves only that no exception escaped. Name the expected value so a failure shows what changed.

sections.title: Boundaries reveal defects
sections.body: Choose cases at the edges: zero, the exact threshold, an empty collection, and the largest accepted value. Ordinary cases confirm the happy path, while boundary cases catch comparisons that are off by one and formatting that drops a leading zero.

sections.title: Absence is not zero
sections.body: None represents a deliberate absence, while zero is a real number. A safe division returns None for a zero divisor and the quotient otherwise. A broad try/except can hide unrelated defects, so catch only the failure the function can handle.

steps.title: Divide safely
steps.prompt: Edit report.py. safe_divide returns None when the divisor is zero and the quotient otherwise.

files.content:
def safe_divide(left, right):
    return left / right
